translationRepairs: Early in Zhonghe, Yang Fuguang of Zhongwu raised troops at Cai; Jian and townsman Wang Jian marched with Lu Yanhong to relieve the capital.

At the beginning of the Tang dynasty's Zhonghe era, Yang Fuguang, military supervisor of the Zhongwu Army, raised troops at Cai. Qin Zongquan sent his general Lu Yanhong to join him; Han Jian and his fellow townsman Wang Jian then joined Yanhong's army and entered the capital to reinforce it.
The proposed correction is substantively warranted by the Chinese, but the replacement needed clearer, more complete English and consistent title terminology.
Yanhong made himself acting commissioner and made Jian Shu prefecture military commissioner.
Yanhong made himself acting commissioner and made Jian prefect of Shu Commandery.
刺史 is a prefect, not a military commissioner; the English also fuses Jian with the place Shu. The cited Chinese directly supports the proposed correction.
He labeled household goods with his name until he learned to read.
He had the names of vessels, beds, and couches written on them and, once familiar with the labels, gradually learned to read.
各題其名 means each object's own name was labeled so Jian could learn characters, not that goods were labeled with his personal name. The cited Chinese directly supports the proposed correction.
Qianning 2 he marched with Maozhen and Xingyu on the capital, forced Wang Gong on Hezhong, and killed ministers.

In Qianning 2 Jian joined Li Maozhen of Fengxiang and Wang Xingyu of Binzhou in marching troops to the capital. They pressured Emperor Zhaozong to appoint Wang Gong military governor of Hezhong and killed senior ministers in the capital.
The proposed correction is substantively warranted by the Chinese, but the replacement needed clearer, more complete English and consistent title terminology.
Month 4, year 3, imperial princes attacked Maozhen, were beaten, and the emperor reached Wei Bridge.
In the fourth month of year 3, Emperor Zhaozong sent the Princes of Yan and Tong at the head of the palace troops to attack Li Maozhen. Maozhen defeated them, and the emperor fled to Wei Bridge.
The proposed correction is substantively warranted by the Chinese, but the replacement needed clearer, more complete English and consistent title terminology.

In the second month of the fourth year, someone came to Jian reporting that Prince Mu and eight other princes below him plotted to kill Jian; Jian imprisoned the eight princes in a separate residence, discharged the twenty thousand rear palace-guard troops accompanying the emperor, and killed Pengri column chief Li Yun.

In the second month of the fourth year, someone came to Jian reporting that the eight princes from Prince Mu downward plotted to kill Jian; Jian imprisoned the eight princes in a separate residence, discharged the twenty thousand rear palace-guard troops accompanying the emperor, and killed Pengri column chief Li Yun.
睦王已下八王 is eight princes counted from Prince Mu down, not Prince Mu plus eight others. The cited Chinese directly supports the proposed correction.
In the eighth month Jian surrounded the Sixteen Residences with troops; Prince Tong and eleven other princes below him were all killed at Shidi Valley, reported as a treason plot.
In the eighth month Jian surrounded the Sixteen Residences with troops; the eleven princes from Prince Tong downward were all killed at Shidi Valley, reported as a treason plot.
通王以下十一王 is eleven princes from Prince Tong down, not Prince Tong plus eleven others. The cited Chinese directly supports the proposed correction.
Sim Ye surrendered Tongzhou; the Founder besieged Hua and Jian surrendered.
The vanguard reached Tongzhou, where Jian's staff officer Sima Ye surrendered the city. The Founder then shifted his army against Huazhou, and Jian, afraid, begged to surrender.
The proposed correction is substantively warranted by the Chinese, but the replacement needed clearer, more complete English and consistent title terminology.
Old army brothers, they reconciled and Jian became Xu commissioner.
They had long been bound as brothers-in-arms. On seeing Jian, his anger quickly subsided, and before long he petitioned for Jian to be appointed military governor of Xu Prefecture.
The Chinese supports the correction, but this wording preserves the subject and title accurately without introducing a misleading standalone name surface.
(The 《Five Dynasties Institutes》 records limited court appearances as special favor.)

Guangqi opened with Shuang campaigning against Zongquan and posting Hanzhi at Song.

At the beginning of Guangqi, Emperor Xizong appointed Zhuge Shuang commander of the campaign forces on the southeastern front against Qin Zongquan. Shuang then petitioned for Hanzhi to serve as his deputy and sent him with troops to garrison Song Prefecture.

After Shuang died Liu Jing held Luoyang and feared Hanzhi.
